ops.title: 2026-07-14 yasyf-home FP bridge outage — b.sock wedged/unbindable after companion-app death; acct-12..16 retreated to symlink as the unblock; acct-11 left on FP with upstream sync queued
ops.body:
2026-07-14 on yasyf-home (ccp v0.53.0, app cask 0.52.0): all 6 hostsync-materialized FP accounts (acct-11..16, created Jul 13 22:11+ by the origin-owned-sync migration) served enumeration but failed content materialization (EDEADLK, files SF_DATALESS). acct-11 only "worked" because a 02:38 session had fully hydrated it. Root sequence: the CCPoolStatus companion app died at 04:21 and the daemon-side group-container bridge (b.sock in `SXKCTF23Q2.ccp`) wedged — still holding the socket but serving nothing; after a daemon restart the bind fails outright with the misleading "awaiting app-group-container consent" hint even though TCC AppData rows for `/Users/yasyf/.cc-pool/bin/cc-pool` exist (written Jul 13 22:12 PDT — note `datetime(...,'unixepoch')` prints UTC; don't misread TCC timestamps). `ccp fp repair` (re-register) does NOT fix a dead bridge; `ccp fp onboard` spins at "waiting for the CCPoolStatus app" even while the app serves domains.sock.

**Why:** distinguishes the three FP failure layers — domain replica (fp repair fixes), daemon bridge (only a working bind fixes), TCC consent (only actually missing on true first-run/upgrade) — and records that the consent hint can be a misdiagnosis.

**How to apply:** for FP reads failing on never-hydrated accounts, `ccp fp repair --retreat --account N` is the safe unblock when the account is all-dataless + session-free (nothing local to lose). Leave hydrated live-session FP accounts alone (their reads work; upstream sync queues until the bridge heals). Afterward accounts sit on symlink until `ccp migrate --to fileprovider` — only re-migrate after the bridge bug is fixed. Full incident: cc-notes note "yasyf-home FP bridge outage 2026-07-14". Related: [[fp-backend-rollout]], [[origin-owned-sync-shipped-v0530]], [[macos-tcc-identifier-keying]].
